questions.stem: To test for a non-reducing sugar, a student must first boil the sample with hydrochloric acid and then neutralise it before adding Benedict's reagent. Why is the acid step necessary?

options.text: The acid activates Benedict's reagent so it works at a higher temperature
The acid hydrolyses the non-reducing sugar into reducing sugars that can then be detected
The acid breaks down proteins into amino acids
The acid removes lipids that would interfere with the test

questions.explanation: Non-reducing sugars like sucrose do not react directly with Benedict's reagent. Boiling with acid hydrolyses the glycosidic bond, breaking the disaccharide into its component monosaccharides, which are reducing sugars and will give a positive Benedict's test.
